clue.text: Part of a big organisation that is wooden

blocks.note: first meaning: a local office or division of a bank or chain
second meaning: a limb of a tree, which is made of wood

explanation.surface: Some department of a large company is described as stiff and wooden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is wooden' reads like a jibe at a dull department, but it simply describes a tree limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank or shop chain has local offices called by this name, and a tree's woody limb shares it.

clue.text: Able lad composed poetic work

indicators.note: to compose is to put together or arrange, so the letters are set in a fresh order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, taken together

explanation.surface: A talented boy wrote a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' looks like the verb for writing the poem; it signals the rearrangement of the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballade is a verse form of three stanzas plus an envoi, each ending with the same refrain line.

clue.text: Monk and a couple of bishops with holy books

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, twice
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A monk and two bishops are carrying scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the monk is the definition and the rest builds him: one A, two Bs and the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a monastery is himself a monk, so the general word stands for this senior example.

clue.text: Pardon prisoner that has cheated

blocks.note: a con is a convict
to have done someone is to have swindled them

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a pardon for an inmate who has been dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Done' in the sense of cheated is informal British usage: 'I've been done' means 'I've been swindled'.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook or forgive an offence, letting it pass without punishment, is a near synonym of excusing it.

clue.text: Try to block drop of rain with plug

indicators.note: a blockage sits inside a passage, so one piece is lodged within the other

blocks.note: to have a go is to try
light rain is said to spit

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to stop a raindrop leaking by using a stopper.
explanation.walkthrough: When it is 'spitting', only a few drops of rain are falling, so a spit is a single drop.
explanation.definitionFit: A small peg or stopper used to close the vent hole of a cask is exactly a plug.

clue.text: Teller of horror stories to attempt verse

blocks.note: Edgar Allan Poe wrote tales of terror
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A writer of horror stories decides to have a go at writing verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Poe also wrote poems such as The Raven, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is metrical writing in lines, the general term for poems as opposed to prose.

clue.text: Set to spark off explosive material

blocks.note: a jelly sets or gels
to ignite is to set alight

explanation.surface: Something is primed to set off a load of explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like 'ready', but it is the jelly sense of firming up.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a blasting compound made of nitroglycerine in a jelly base, used in quarrying and demolition.

clue.text: Hide in this processing plant

blocks.note: surface reading: an invitation to take cover inside a factory
setter's reading: hide is animal skin, and this is where skins are processed into leather

explanation.surface: Someone is told to conceal themselves in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a verb telling you to conceal yourself; it is the noun for an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw skins are treated with tannin there to turn them into leather, so it is a plant processing them.

clue.text: Fantastic Leicester won – a song for the spectators?

indicators.note: something fantastic is fanciful and unreal, so the letters take an imagined new form

blocks.note: the letters of these two words
taken as written, added to the mix

explanation.surface: A football fan celebrates Leicester's amazing win and asks what the crowd should sing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' belongs to the letters being rearranged, not to the definition. The question mark marks the definition as an example: the crowd song is one of many.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Diamond's hit is a stadium singalong, belted out by crowds at football grounds and ballparks.

clue.text: Card for social organisation

blocks.note: first meaning: a playing card of the suit with a black trefoil
second meaning: a society of members who meet together

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a membership card for a society; the two nouns are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both one of the four playing-card suits and a society whose members meet for a shared interest.

clue.text: Fresh enthusiasm comes with an introduction to delightful country

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the very start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: fresh means new
zeal is eager enthusiasm
taken as written
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A traveller arriving in a lovely country feels a renewed burst of keenness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delightful country' looks like the definition, but 'delightful' only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pacific island nation, made up of two main islands south-east of Australia, is a country.

clue.text: Socialist leader, a sort disturbed by Conservative

indicators.note: things disturbed are knocked out of place, so these letters are moved around

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A left-wing leader is described as the type to be upset by a right-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation goes first even though 'Conservative' comes last in the clue: 'by' only means 'next to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro led Cuba's communist revolution and ran the country for decades as a socialist head of state.

clue.text: Tea? Good, about to come in before expected time!

indicators.note: whatever comes in enters something else, so these letters go inside the outer word

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
re means about, concerning
early means ahead of time

explanation.surface: A host offers tea and is pleased that a guest is coming in ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just the first word; 'about' is the abbreviation RE, as in letter headings, not a sign of reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: This blend of black leaves flavoured with bergamot oil is a well-known variety of the drink.

clue.text: Remorse of English fool interrupting Trump's no.2

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so these letters split the outer word

blocks.note: a nit is a nitwit, a fool
E is the abbreviation for English
Mike Pence was vice-president in Trump's first term

explanation.surface: An English idiot butts in on the US vice-president, then feels sorry about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The vice-president's surname is broken after its first two letters to admit the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrow and regret for wrongdoing, the feeling of repentance, is the same as remorse.

clue.text: Not well, say, with friend going against the law

blocks.note: not well means sick
e.g. means for example, as does say
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A sick person and a pal are breaking the law together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is the usual crossword signal for EG, both meaning 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a manner forbidden by statute is acting unlawfully, contrary to the legal rules.

clue.text: Very small container by end of alleyway

indicators.note: the end is the final part, so just the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: a tin is a container
the closing letter of this word

explanation.surface: A little box sits at the far end of a narrow lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very small' looks as if it describes the container; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something minute or minuscule is extremely little, the same sense as the two-word phrase.

clue.text: Metal left inside idol

indicators.note: inside places one thing within another, so a letter sits in the middle of a word

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
an idol is a false god

explanation.surface: A metal object has been placed within a statue of a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: The golden idol of the surface hints at the answer, which is fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow precious element is one of the metals, prized for jewellery and coinage.

clue.text: Somehow hairy dog ate end of the stew

indicators.note: somehow means in some unknown manner, so the letters come out in an unexpected arrangement
the end is the final part, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: the letters of these two words
the closing letter of the phrase

explanation.surface: A shaggy dog has somehow managed to eat the last of the stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hairy' looks like it describes the dog, but it is the definition, in an unusual sense: having a chin beard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing a small pointed tuft of beard on the chin is literally hairy there, an adjective formed from that beard.

clue.text: Worn out fellow going round kept going for ages

indicators.note: to go round something is to encircle it, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
ragged means worn and tattered

explanation.surface: A tired man goes on his rounds after working for a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn out fellow' wants to be read as one tired man; the fellow is an academic who wraps around the tatters.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting that continued tediously for far too long is said to have done this, an idiom for tedious prolonging.

clue.text: Cook's device beginning to give problem?

indicators.note: a beginning is the start of something, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
a riddle is a puzzle or problem

explanation.surface: A chef wonders whether their kitchen gadget is starting to play up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning to give problem' reads as a machine starting to fail; it is the first letter of 'give' plus a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat iron plate heated for making pancakes and flatbreads is a piece of kitchen equipment.

clue.text: Survive as final batter to get dismissed

blocks.note: a dismissed batter is out
the final one in the batting order is the last

explanation.surface: A cricketer hangs on as the last batter before the innings ends.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batter who is out last has stayed longer than all the others, so the wordplay also hints at the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To live or last longer than someone else is to survive them, a close synonym.

clue.text: Like the proverbial bird you want being dealt with

definitions.text: Like the proverbial bird you want

blocks.clueFragment: Like the proverbial bird you want
blocks.note: first meaning: 'a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush', so the bird worth having is held
second meaning: a matter under control and being handled

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says a sure thing you already hold beats two uncertain ones still out in the bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both held in your grasp, as the proverb's bird is, and currently under attention or control.

clue.text: False alarm – drinking spirit insignificant

indicators.note: something false is not genuine, so these letters are a counterfeit arrangement
a drinker takes something in, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: the letters of this word
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A false alarm caused by someone's drinking proves to be of no importance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False alarm' reads as a set phrase, but 'False' works on the letters of the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something minor or of small importance, only at the edges of what matters, is unimportant.

clue.text: Move home location, from what we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the letters are written as they sound

blocks.note: home is IN, a location is a SITE

explanation.surface: Someone moves house and reports a rumour about the new place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move home' looks like a phrase about relocating, but 'Move' alone is the definition in the sense of stirring someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir or urge people into action is to provoke them, one sense of the verb meaning to rouse.

clue.text: Cold maiden? Provide blanket maybe

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored

explanation.surface: A chilly young woman needs someone to give her a blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' suggests a girl, but in cricket a maiden is a scoreless set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying a blanket over someone is one example of shielding them, hence 'maybe' in the definition.

clue.text: We p-picked up some information – rest may be this

blocks.note: taken as written
picked up information means learned, and the stammered 'p-p' tells us to stammer the first letter too

explanation.surface: We stammer that after picking up knowledge, a break must be due.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in 'p-picked' is the instruction: the word for picked up is said with its first letter doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest after hard work is one deserved by effort, which is what the adjective describes.

clue.text: Have a look – find hidden meat

indicators.note: something concealed is tucked away within other words, waiting to be uncovered

blocks.note: the letters run across the last two of 'Have', 'a' and the first of 'look'

explanation.surface: Someone peers around and discovers some meat that was stashed away.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles three words, starting inside the first and ending with the start of the last.
explanation.definitionFit: The flesh of a calf eaten as food is a kind of meat.

clue.text: Dull commercials showing nymphs

blocks.note: dry means dull, uninteresting
ads are advertisements

explanation.surface: Boring television adverts feature woodland spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing' looks like part of the advertising picture, but it only joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these were tree spirits, a class of nymph living in woods and oaks.

clue.text: City brute running wild – one to be caught

indicators.note: running wild means out of control, so these letters scatter into a new order
whatever is caught is held inside, so a letter is enclosed by the others

blocks.note: the letters of this word
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A savage is rampaging through a city and must be captured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One to be caught' sounds like a wanted criminal; it is the numeral placed inside the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital of Lebanon, a Mediterranean port and a major city of the Middle East.
